Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern has non-private constructor. (SING_SINGLETON_HAS_NONPRIVATE_CONSTRUCTOR)
Bug_Details:
This class is using singleton design pattern and has non-private constructor (please note that a default constructor might exist which is not private). Given that, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
The easier solution would be making the constructor private.
SEI CERT MSC07-J rule
Bug_Explanation: The Singleton class implements the singleton design pattern, but the constructor is not private, which allows multiple instances of the class to be created, violating the singleton pattern.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by creating a new instance of the Singleton class using the public constructor, which violates the singleton pattern. This is done in the testSingletonPattern method on line 10 and in the testShowBug method by calling the showBug method, which creates two new instances of the Singleton class.
